answer: Bonded staking registries mitigate Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock scarce capital at an admission inlet before engaging in market coordination. Anchoring identity issuance to this economic wharf forces an attacker to bear the verifiable opportunity cost of illiquid tokens per clone, rather than spamming the transaction river for free. A key limitation is that deep-pocketed adversaries can still subsidize multiple identities, which disproportionately penalizes low-capital agents.
